Definition: from G1443; Hebraic or the Jewish language:--Hebrew.
BiblicalUsage: Hebraikos means Hebrew, of the Jewish language, and it appears once, in the inscription over the cross. In Luke 23:38 the title was written in Greek and Latin and Hebrew, and this is the word for the Hebrew part of it. The older Greek text behind the King James carries the three languages here, while the shorter text used by modern editions leaves the list out.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the three languages on that board matter: the King of the Jews was announced to the whole world, in the tongue of the empire, the tongue of the law, and the tongue of the people.
